prompt: Why is so much Svelte 4 code still running and still being written?
hint: What does the Svelte 5 compiler do with an old component?

choices.text: Svelte 5 is still in beta, so most projects wait for the final release
choices.why: Svelte 5 was released in October 2024.

choices.text: Svelte 5 still compiles it, in legacy mode
choices.why: Right, so projects upgrade the compiler first and the components one at a time.

choices.text: Svelte 4 components run faster, so teams keep them on purpose
choices.why: Speed is not the reason the lesson gives; the gradual upgrade is.

choices.text: Browsers refuse runes unless a flag is switched on
choices.why: Browsers never see runes; the compiler removes them.

prompt: Match each Svelte 4 spelling with its Svelte 5 equivalent.
hint: The table at the start of the lesson.

prompt: What changed about stores between Svelte 4 and Svelte 5?
hint: Read the paragraph under the table.

choices.text: They were removed, and `$store` is now an error
choices.why: They work exactly as before.

choices.text: They became runes: `$writable` replaces `writable`
choices.why: There is no such rune.

choices.text: Nothing; runes in `.svelte.js` now cover many of the same cases
choices.why: Right. Lesson 10 is about choosing between them.

choices.text: They only work in legacy-mode components
choices.why: They work in runes components too.

prompt: A project has runes components and legacy components. Which statement is true?
hint: The mode is decided per file.

choices.text: They can use each other; each file is in one mode
choices.why: Right, which is what makes a gradual upgrade possible.

choices.text: A runes component may use `export let` as long as it also uses `$state`
choices.why: In runes mode `export let` is an error.

choices.text: A legacy component may use runes if it imports them from `svelte`
choices.why: Runes are not available in legacy mode, imported or not.

choices.text: A runes page cannot render a legacy child at all
choices.why: The planner's page did exactly that with `WeekNav`.

prompt: In SvelteKit 3, `import { page } from '$app/stores'` becomes `import { page } from '$app/___'`.
hint: The module named after what runes hold.

prompt: What does `<svelte:options runes={false} />` at the top of `WeekNav.svelte` do?
hint: The project's configuration forces runes.

choices.text: Turns runes off for the whole project
choices.why: It applies to this one file only.

choices.text: Puts this one file in legacy mode
choices.why: Right. Without it the project's setting forces runes and the file is an error.

choices.text: Stops the component from re-rendering when its props change
choices.why: It chooses a compilation mode; it says nothing about updates.

choices.text: Marks the component as server-only, so it never reaches the browser
choices.why: The buttons worked in the browser, so it reached it.

prompt: With the options line deleted, the terminal shows `legacy_export_invalid`. What is the compiler saying?
hint: Read the message's second half.

choices.text: The `week.js` import path is wrong
choices.why: The error points at line 4, `export let week;`.

choices.text: Props must be exported with `export const` in Svelte 5
choices.why: The message names `$props()`, not `export const`.

choices.text: `export let` is Svelte 4 syntax, refused in runes mode; use `$props()`
choices.why: Right, and the message names the replacement itself.

choices.text: The development server crashed and has to be restarted
choices.why: It kept running and answered `500 GET /`.

prompt: How does the runes page learn that `WeekNav` moved the week?
hint: Look at the one line the page uses.

choices.text: Through `bind:week`, which the page added
choices.why: There is no binding in that line.

choices.text: `on:change`, with the week in `event.detail`
choices.why: Right: the dispatcher sends it and the Svelte 4 syntax listens.

choices.text: The two share the module `week.js`, which holds the current week as state
choices.why: `week.js` holds plain functions and no state.

choices.text: It reads `WeekNav`'s `shown` variable after each click
choices.why: A parent cannot read a child's variables.

prompt: The page with the legacy `WeekNav` printed the same tree as lesson 3's page. Why?
hint: What does `look` see?

choices.text: `look` caches pages it has seen
choices.why: It opens a fresh browser each time.

choices.text: The legacy component was ignored and the old markup shown instead
choices.why: The paragraph was replaced by `WeekNav`; the buttons are its own.

choices.text: The markup is the same; the mode does not show from outside
choices.why: Right.

prompt: How does a Svelte 4 `$:` statement decide when to run again?
hint: When is it decided?

choices.text: From the names written in it, read once at build time
choices.why: Right, and reads elsewhere are invisible to it.

choices.text: From what it reads each time it runs, like a derived value
choices.why: That is the Svelte 5 rule.

choices.text: It runs again on every change to any variable in the component
choices.why: It is narrower than that, and the narrowness is the bug.

choices.text: It runs on a timer, sixty times a second
choices.why: Nothing in Svelte polls.

prompt: After `$: shown = describe();` and two presses of `Next week`, what did the page show?
hint: Compare the label with the add button.

choices.text: An error, because `describe` is not reactive
choices.why: No error at all: that is the trouble.

choices.text: Week of 2 Nov 2026, and every course at 0 minutes
choices.why: The totals moved, but the label did not.

choices.text: The week of 19 October everywhere, since the clicks did nothing
choices.why: The add button said 2 Nov 2026: the week did change.

choices.text: The old label beside a total of 0
choices.why: Right: the week moved, the label stayed at 19 October.

prompt: Why does `let shown = $derived(describe());` update where the `$:` version did not?
hint: Runes track what code does.

choices.text: `$derived` re-runs on every click in the component
choices.why: It re-runs when something it read changes, not on clicks.

choices.text: It records `label` and `week` as `describe` reads them
choices.why: Right. Reads inside the function count.

choices.text: The compiler inlines the function body into the expression before reading its names
choices.why: Nothing is inlined; the tracking happens at runtime.

prompt: Put the story of the stuck label in order.
hint: The compiler's decision comes before any click.
items: The compiler reads `$: shown = describe();` and finds only `describe`
It decides the statement never needs to run again
A click changes `week` and the page receives it
trap: Everything after the build is the consequence of a decision taken at build time.

prompt: What does `node migrate.mjs src/lib/WeekNav.svelte` do to the file?
hint: Read the script's last line.

choices.text: Rewrites it in place and keeps a backup beside it
choices.why: It writes to standard output and nowhere else.

choices.text: Nothing; it prints the rewritten component
choices.why: Right, so you can read it before deciding.

choices.text: Deletes it and creates `WeekNav.svelte5`
choices.why: No file is created or deleted.

choices.text: Compiles it to JavaScript, as `compile.mjs` does, but for Svelte 4
choices.why: It produces Svelte 5 source, not JavaScript.

prompt: What did the migrator leave for you to change by hand? Choose all that apply.
hint: Decisions, plus one line it does not touch.

choices.text: The `<svelte:options runes={false} />` line
choices.why: Yes: left in place, it would put the result back in legacy mode.

choices.text: `createEventDispatcher` and `dispatch`
choices.why: Yes: replacing them means changing every parent too.

choices.text: `week = $bindable()`, kept because the old component assigned to its prop
choices.why: Yes: the planner chose a callback instead.

choices.text: `on:click`, which it left alone
choices.why: No: it became `onclick`.

prompt: Why does the finished `WeekNav` take an `onchange` callback rather than a bindable `week`?
hint: Who owns the week?

choices.text: Bindable props were removed in Svelte 5
choices.why: `$bindable` exists; the migrator produced one.

choices.text: A callback is faster than a binding
choices.why: Speed is not the argument the lesson makes.

choices.text: The component only has to tell its parent which week comes next; the page owns the week
choices.why: Right. Lesson 5 is about when each is right.

choices.text: `onchange` is the only prop name the browser delivers to components
choices.why: A callback prop can have any name; the browser is not involved.

prompt: To run the same rewrite over every component of a project, the command is `npx sv ___ svelte-5`.
hint: The verb, as the script's name has it.

prompt: The old page fails with `module_removed_lib`. What does the message offer besides `#lib`?
hint: For a project with a lot of old code.

choices.text: An alias in the SvelteKit config to keep `$lib`
choices.why: Right. For a new project, change the import instead.

choices.text: A command that rewrites every import in the project
choices.why: It names a configuration option, not a command.

choices.text: A downgrade to SvelteKit 2
choices.why: Nothing in it suggests going back.

choices.text: Moving `week.js` into `src/routes`, where `$lib` still works
choices.why: `$lib` works nowhere in SvelteKit 3 without the alias.

prompt: Why did `$app/stores` fail with a stack trace while rendering, when `$lib` failed before the page was built?
hint: One of the two modules still exists.

choices.text: Because `$app/stores` was imported second
choices.why: It was imported first; order is not the reason.

choices.text: `$app/stores` still exists and throws when read; `$lib` is refused when imports are resolved
choices.why: Right: one is a missing module, the other a module whose exports throw.

choices.text: Stores only fail in the browser, never on the server
choices.why: This one failed on the server, during rendering.

prompt: An example you found uses `$state`, `onclick` and `$lib/`. What is it written for?
hint: Svelte and SvelteKit are dated separately.

choices.text: Svelte 4 with SvelteKit 1
choices.why: `$state` and `onclick` are Svelte 5.

choices.text: Svelte 5 with SvelteKit 3
choices.why: SvelteKit 3 refuses `$lib`; it writes `#lib`.

choices.text: Svelte 5 with SvelteKit 2
choices.why: Right: runes, and the alias SvelteKit 3 removed.

prompt: Why does code suggested by a language model so often mix Svelte 4 and Svelte 5?
hint: What did it learn from?

choices.text: Models deliberately prefer the older syntax because it is shorter
choices.why: Nothing deliberate; it is what they read.

choices.text: It learnt from what was written, and most Svelte ever written is Svelte 4
choices.why: Right. Read the error, find the line in the table, change the spelling.

choices.text: The compiler accepts any mixture, so nobody notices
choices.why: It refuses legacy syntax in runes mode, with an error.

choices.text: Svelte 5 documentation still uses Svelte 4 examples
choices.why: The lesson blames the training data, not the documentation.

prompt: Match each message with what caused it.
hint: Three errors from this lesson.
right_distractors: A `$:` statement that depends on nothing

prompt: In "What `$:` got wrong", the week started on 19 October and `Next week` was pressed twice. On which day of November did the new week start?
hint: Add fourteen days to 19 October.

prompt: In the legacy `WeekNav`, where does the new week travel inside the `change` event?
hint: Read the `on:change` handler in the page.

choices.text: In `event.target.value`, like an input
choices.why: A component event has no target input; the dispatcher puts it in `detail`.

choices.text: In `event.detail.week`
choices.why: Right: `dispatch('change', { week })` puts it there.

choices.text: In a global variable that both components import from `week.js`
choices.why: `week.js` exports functions, no shared variable.

choices.text: Nowhere: the page reads the label text back from the DOM
choices.why: The page never reads the DOM; it receives the value.

prompt: Why does the lesson put the old code at `src/routes/old/+page.svelte`?
hint: What would break otherwise?

choices.text: Old code is only allowed in a folder called `old`
choices.why: The name is arbitrary; any folder makes a page.

choices.text: To test it on a page of its own without breaking the planner
choices.why: Right. The folder is deleted afterwards.

choices.text: So that SvelteKit compiles it in legacy mode automatically
choices.why: Nothing about the folder changes the mode; the errors show it did not.

prompt: What is the quickest reliable way to turn a pasted Svelte 4 snippet into Svelte 5?
hint: Each refusal names its replacement.

choices.text: Turn off runes in `vite.config.js` for the whole project
choices.why: That keeps the old spelling everywhere instead of converting it.

choices.text: Delete every `$:` line and hope the page still updates
choices.why: Deleting is not converting; the derived values would be gone.

choices.text: Run `migrate`, then fix what each error names
choices.why: Right, then finish the decisions the migrator leaves.

choices.text: Wrap the snippet in `<svelte:options runes={true} />`
choices.why: That forces runes mode, which turns the old syntax into errors, not into Svelte 5.
